# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Namour_2015_filgotinib"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Namour_2015_filgotinib"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-015-0240-z> (open access, PMC4513223)

Filgotinib (GLPG0634) is an oral selective JAK1 inhibitor. It is converted to
an active metabolite whose plasma exposure is 16- to 20-fold higher than that of
the parent but which is less potent. Namour 2015 fitted a joint population
PK model for filgotinib and the metabolite. The pharmacodynamic biomarker was ex
vivo IL-6-induced STAT1 phosphorylation (pSTAT1) in CD4+ lymphocytes, and the
paper modelled it as a direct, complete inhibition driven by both moieties.
Simulations of this model supported the 200 mg/day ceiling of the phase IIB
DARWIN programme in rheumatoid arthritis.

# Population

The PK model was fitted to 56 healthy male volunteers (40-60 years, BMI
18-30 kg/m^2) from two phase I studies (NCT01179581, NCT01419990). They took
single doses of 25-200 mg or ten days of 25, 50 or 100 mg twice daily or
200, 300 or 450 mg once daily, as capsules after a standard breakfast. Sparse
samples from 24 methotrexate-inadequate-responder patients with rheumatoid
arthritis (RA) were added. These patients took 100 mg twice daily or 200 mg once
daily in a phase IIa study (NCT01384422; 33 of the 36 enrolled patients were
female). The pSTAT1 PK/PD model uses only the phase I data. Study designs are in
Namour 2015 Table 1. The paper does not tabulate body weight.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Namour_2015_filgotinib")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source; the
table below collects them. Namour 2015 Tables 4 and 5 print the log-transformed
parameters on the log scale and FRAC on the probit scale. The model stores
those transformed values unchanged.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` | -0.733 (ka = 0.480 1/h) | Table 4, ka (log) |
| `lcl` | 3.97 (CL_P/F = 53.0 L/h) | Table 4, CLP/F (log) |
| `lvc` | 3.08 (V_C/F = 21.8 L) | Table 4, VC/F (log) |
| `lq` | 2.02 (Q/F = 7.54 L/h) | Table 4, Q/F (log) |
| `lvp` | 4.72 (V_P/F = 112 L) | Table 4, VP/F (log) |
| `lcl_metab` | 1.04 (CL_M/F = 2.83 L/h) | Table 4, CLM/F (log) |
| `lvc_metab` | 4.36 (V_M/F = 78.3 L) | Table 4, VM/F (log) |
| `probitfm_dose300` | 0.375 (fm = 0.646) | Table 4, FRAC300 mg (probit) |
| `probitfm_dose450` | 0.363 (fm = 0.642) | Table 4, FRAC450 mg (probit) |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.679 | Table 4, Effect of weight |
| `e_sexf_vc` | 2.95 | Table 4, Effect of sex |
| `e_dis_ra_fdepot` | 0.216 | Table 4, Relative increase in bioavailability in RA patients |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc`, `etalcl_metab`, `etalvc_metab` | 0.102, 2.55, 0.0444, 0.0418 | Table 4, BSV variance column |
| `propSd`, `propSd_metab` | sqrt(0.337), sqrt(0.0726) | Table 4, sigma2 P,prop and M,prop |
| `rbase`, `etarbase` | 22.3 %, 117 %^2 (normal) | Table 5, pSTAT1BL |
| `lic50`, `etalic50` | 5.68 (IC50_P = 293 ng/mL), 1.87 | Table 5, log IC50,P |
| `lic50_metab`, `etalic50_metab` | 7.43 (IC50_M = 1686 ng/mL), 0.106 | Table 5, log IC50,M |
| `lhill` | 0.680 (H = 1.97) | Table 5, log H |
| `addSd_pstat1`, `propSd_pstat1` | sqrt(2.11), sqrt(0.198) | Table 5, residual variance rows |
| PK ODEs | n/a | Eq. 1; Fig. 3 |
| fm = 1 below 300 mg/day | n/a | Results: secondary pathway only at doses at and above 300 mg |
| pSTAT1 = BL (1 - (C0P + C0M) / (1 + C0P + C0M)), C0x = (Cx/IC50x)^H | n/a | Eq. 2 |

# Typical-value replication of the pSTAT1 simulations (Tables 6-8, Figure 8)

Namour 2015 simulated steady-state pSTAT1 inhibition over a dosing interval for
a typical 75 kg male healthy volunteer. Inhibition is expressed relative to the
baseline: `100 * (1 - pSTAT1 / pSTAT1_BL)`. Table 6 gives the result with both
moieties; Tables 7 and 8 give the hypothetical inhibition from filgotinib alone
or from the metabolite alone. The same quantities are computed below from the
typical-value model, with dosing for ten days so that the metabolite
(half-life about 20 h) has reached steady state.

```{r typical-sim}
mod <- readModelDb("Namour_2015_filgotinib")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
typ <- rxode2::rxode(mod)

# Typical-value solves over several subjects (one per regimen or covariate
# case) are intended here; mute only rxode2's notice that the multi-subject
# solve has no between-subject variability.
solve_typical <- function(events, ...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events, returnType = "data.frame", ...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}

regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,  ~amt, ~ii,
  "30 q.d.",   30,  24,
  "50 q.d.",   50,  24,
  "100 q.d.", 100,  24,
  "100 b.i.d.", 100, 12,
  "200 q.d.", 200,  24,
  "300 q.d.", 300,  24
) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()), daily = amt * 24 / ii)

make_typical <- function(r) {
  n_dose <- 240 / r$ii
  last <- (n_dose - 1) * r$ii
  doses <- tibble(time = seq(0, last, by = r$ii), amt = r$amt, evid = 1L,
                  cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- tibble(time = seq(last, last + r$ii, by = 0.05), amt = 0, evid = 0L,
                cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(id = r$id, regimen = r$regimen, WT = 75, SEXF = 0, DIS_RA = 0,
           DOSE_FILGOTINIB_MGD = r$daily, tau_start = last) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid))
}
ev_typ <- bind_rows(lapply(split(regimens, regimens$id), make_typical))

sim_typ <- solve_typical(ev_typ, keep = c("regimen", "tau_start"))

bl <- typ$theta[["rbase"]]
ic50_p <- exp(typ$theta[["lic50"]])
ic50_m <- exp(typ$theta[["lic50_metab"]])
hill <- exp(typ$theta[["lhill"]])

inh <- sim_typ |>
  mutate(
    both = 100 * (1 - pstat1 / bl),
    parent_alone = 100 * (Cc / ic50_p)^hill / (1 + (Cc / ic50_p)^hill),
    metab_alone = 100 * (Cc_metab / ic50_m)^hill / (1 + (Cc_metab / ic50_m)^hill)
  )

inh_summary <- inh |>
  pivot_longer(c(both, parent_alone, metab_alone), names_to = "source", values_to = "inh") |>
  group_by(regimen, source) |>
  summarise(Minimum = min(inh), Maximum = max(inh), Mean = mean(inh), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r table-6}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,     ~source,        ~Minimum, ~Maximum, ~Mean,
  "30 q.d.",    "both",           3.44,     27.6,    8.86,
  "50 q.d.",    "both",           9.11,     50.9,    20.1,
  "100 q.d.",   "both",           28.2,     80.1,    47.4,
  "100 b.i.d.", "both",           71.6,     87.0,    78.5,
  "200 q.d.",   "both",           61.8,     94.5,    77.6,
  "300 q.d.",   "both",           60.3,     97.3,    77.1,
  # Table 7 prints '<0.1' for the filgotinib-alone minimum of the q.d. arms;
  # those cells are NA here.
  "30 q.d.",    "parent_alone",     NA,     24.2,    2.31,
  "50 q.d.",    "parent_alone",     NA,     46.4,    4.99,
  "100 q.d.",   "parent_alone",     NA,     77.2,    10.6,
  "100 b.i.d.", "parent_alone",  0.427,     78.0,    22.2,
  "200 q.d.",   "parent_alone",  0.128,     93.6,    17.5,
  "300 q.d.",   "parent_alone",  0.295,     97.1,    21.9,
  "30 q.d.",    "metab_alone",    3.42,     9.25,    6.43,
  "50 q.d.",    "metab_alone",    9.06,     21.9,    15.9,
  "100 q.d.",   "metab_alone",    28.1,     53.5,    42.4,
  "100 b.i.d.", "metab_alone",    71.5,     78.7,    75.9,
  "200 q.d.",   "metab_alone",    61.8,     82.8,    75.0,
  "300 q.d.",   "metab_alone",    60.3,     81.7,    73.5
)

cmp_pd <- published |>
  pivot_longer(c(Minimum, Maximum, Mean), names_to = "statistic", values_to = "published") |>
  left_join(
    inh_summary |>
      pivot_longer(c(Minimum, Maximum, Mean), names_to = "statistic", values_to = "simulated"),
    by = c("regimen", "source", "statistic")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    source = factor(source, c("both", "parent_alone", "metab_alone"),
                    c("Both moieties (Table 6)", "Filgotinib alone (Table 7)",
                      "Metabolite alone (Table 8)")),
    regimen = factor(regimen, regimens$regimen),
    statistic = factor(statistic, c("Minimum", "Maximum", "Mean")),
    diff = simulated - published
  ) |>
  arrange(source, regimen, statistic)

cmp_pd |>
  mutate(published = ifelse(is.na(published), "<0.1", formatC(published, digits = 3, format = "fg")),
         simulated = formatC(simulated, digits = 3, format = "fg"),
         diff = ifelse(is.na(diff), "", sprintf("%+.2f", diff))) |>
  rename(Source = source, Regimen = regimen, Statistic = statistic,
         "Published (%)" = published, "Simulated (%)" = simulated,
         "Difference (percentage points)" = diff) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Steady-state pSTAT1 inhibition in a typical 75 kg male: Namour 2015 Tables 6-8 vs the packaged model.")
```

Every cell is within about one percentage point of the published value. The
published values come from simulations that carried 1,000 bootstrap replicates
of parameter uncertainty, so they need not equal a single typical-value
solve exactly. The comparison is deterministic on both sides, so a tight bound
applies:

```{r table-6-check}
stopifnot(
  max(abs(cmp_pd$diff), na.rm = TRUE) < 2,
  # The filgotinib-alone minimum is <0.1% in the q.d. arms (Table 7).
  all(inh_summary$Minimum[inh_summary$source == "parent_alone" &
                            inh_summary$regimen %in% c("30 q.d.", "50 q.d.", "100 q.d.")] < 0.1)
)
```

```{r figure-8, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates Figure 8 of Namour 2015: steady-state pSTAT1 inhibition over one
# dosing interval, with the filgotinib and metabolite concentrations on a
# common arbitrary scale (each divided by its maximum across regimens).
fig8 <- inh |>
  mutate(t = time - tau_start, regimen = factor(regimen, regimens$regimen),
         `Filgotinib (scaled)` = 100 * Cc / max(Cc),
         `Metabolite (scaled)` = 100 * Cc_metab / max(Cc_metab)) |>
  select(regimen, t, `pSTAT1 inhibition (%)` = both, `Filgotinib (scaled)`, `Metabolite (scaled)`) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(regimen, t), names_to = "quantity")

ggplot(fig8, aes(t, value, colour = quantity)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("pSTAT1 inhibition (%)" = "#B2182B",
                                 "Filgotinib (scaled)" = "black",
                                 "Metabolite (scaled)" = "grey55")) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose at steady state (h)", y = "Inhibition (%) / scaled concentration",
       colour = NULL, caption = "Replicates Figure 8 of Namour 2015 (typical subject; no uncertainty band).") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r figure-7}
# Replicates Figure 7 of Namour 2015: typical-subject pSTAT1 response against
# each moiety's concentration with the other moiety absent; vertical lines at
# the IC50 values (293 and 1686 ng/mL).
conc <- 10^seq(0, 4.5, length.out = 200)
fig7 <- bind_rows(
  tibble(moiety = "Filgotinib", conc = conc, ic50 = ic50_p),
  tibble(moiety = "Metabolite", conc = conc, ic50 = ic50_m)
) |>
  mutate(pstat1 = bl / (1 + (conc / ic50)^hill))

ggplot(fig7, aes(conc, pstat1)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = ic50), linetype = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~moiety) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Plasma concentration (ng/mL)", y = "pSTAT1-positive CD4+ cells (%)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 7 of Namour 2015 (typical values; no confidence band).") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Virtual cohort for the phase I studies

The stochastic checks below simulate the phase I healthy-volunteer designs:
single doses of 25-200 mg (Table 2) and ten days of 25, 50 or 100 mg b.i.d. or
200, 300 or 450 mg q.d. (Table 3), with 100 virtual subjects per arm. All
subjects are male healthy volunteers (`SEXF = 0`, `DIS_RA = 0`). The paper does
not report body weight, so weight is drawn from a normal distribution with
mean 75 kg and SD 10 kg, truncated to 55-100 kg. That range is consistent with
the BMI 18-30 kg/m^2 inclusion window, and the mean matches the typical subject
of the paper's simulations. Sampling follows the rich designs of Table 1. Below
the assay LLOQ of 1.00 ng/mL, concentrations are set missing, as the paper
excluded below-LLOQ samples.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20150213)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20150213)
n_per_arm <- 100L

arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,      ~amt, ~ii, ~n_dose, ~design,
  "SD 25 mg",        25,   0,      1, "single",
  "SD 50 mg",        50,   0,      1, "single",
  "SD 100 mg",      100,   0,      1, "single",
  "SD 200 mg",      200,   0,      1, "single",
  "25 mg b.i.d.",    25,  12,     20, "multiple",
  "50 mg b.i.d.",    50,  12,     20, "multiple",
  "100 mg b.i.d.",  100,  12,     20, "multiple",
  "200 mg q.d.",    200,  24,     10, "multiple",
  "300 mg q.d.",    300,  24,     10, "multiple",
  "450 mg q.d.",    450,  24,     10, "multiple"
) |>
  mutate(arm = seq_len(n()),
         daily = ifelse(ii == 0, amt, amt * 24 / ii),
         last = ifelse(ii == 0, 0, (n_dose - 1) * ii))

# Rich nominal sampling after a dose (h); 72 h follow-up after the last dose.
rel_grid <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12,
              16, 20, 24, 30, 36, 48, 60, 72)

make_cohort <- function(a) {
  ids <- (a$arm - 1L) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  wt <- pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_per_arm, 75, 10), 55), 100)
  dose_times <- if (a$ii == 0) 0 else seq(0, a$last, by = a$ii)
  obs_times <- sort(unique(c(rel_grid[rel_grid <= 24], a$last + rel_grid)))
  one <- bind_rows(
    tibble(time = dose_times, amt = a$amt, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_),
    tibble(time = obs_times, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  ) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid))
  tidyr::crossing(tibble(id = ids, WT = wt), one) |>
    mutate(treatment = a$treatment, last = a$last, tau_h = a$ii,
           SEXF = 0, DIS_RA = 0, DOSE_FILGOTINIB_MGD = a$daily) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
events <- bind_rows(lapply(split(arms, arms$arm), make_cohort))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, keep = c("treatment", "last", "tau_h"),
                       returnType = "data.frame")
```

```{r figure-5}
# Replicates Figure 5 of Namour 2015: mean filgotinib and metabolite profiles
# over the first and last dosing interval at 200 mg q.d. (population means of
# the simulated individual predictions; the figure plots population predictions).
sim |>
  filter(treatment == "200 mg q.d.") |>
  mutate(day = ifelse(time < 24, "Day 1", ifelse(time >= last & time <= last + 24, "Day 10", NA)),
         t = ifelse(day == "Day 1", time, time - last)) |>
  filter(!is.na(day)) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cc_metab), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(analyte = ifelse(analyte == "Cc", "Filgotinib", "Metabolite")) |>
  group_by(analyte, day, t) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(conc), lo = quantile(conc, 0.05), hi = quantile(conc, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(t, mean, colour = day, fill = day)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Concentration (ng/mL)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Namour 2015: mean with 5th-95th percentile band, 200 mg q.d.") +
  theme_bw()
```

# PKNCA validation

The NCA is run separately for filgotinib and metabolite. It uses the individual
predictions (no residual error), with values below the LLOQ set missing. The
single-dose arms are analysed from 0 to infinity. The multiple-dose arms are
analysed over the last dosing interval (AUC0-tau, Cmax, Cmin), and the
half-life comes from the 72 h after the last dose. PKNCA warns when a
subject's filgotinib profile falls below the LLOQ too soon to give the three
points it needs for a half-life. Those subjects drop out of the half-life
summary only, much as Table 2 reports the half-life for n = 4-5 of 6 subjects
in several arms.

```{r pknca}
lloq <- 1
run_nca <- function(conc_col) {
  conc <- sim |>
    transmute(id, time, treatment, conc = .data[[conc_col]]) |>
    mutate(conc = ifelse(conc < lloq, NA_real_, conc)) |>
    filter(!is.na(conc))
  # Time-zero anchor: pre-dose concentration is 0 for the first dose.
  conc <- bind_rows(conc, conc |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, conc = 0)) |>
    distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    arrange(id, treatment, time)

  dose_df <- events |>
    filter(evid == 1) |>
    select(id, time, amt, treatment)

  iv_sd <- arms |>
    filter(design == "single") |>
    transmute(treatment, start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
              aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
  iv_md <- arms |>
    filter(design == "multiple") |>
    transmute(treatment, start = last, end = last + ii, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
              auclast = TRUE, cmin = TRUE)
  iv_hl <- arms |>
    filter(design == "multiple") |>
    transmute(treatment, start = last, end = last + 72, half.life = TRUE)
  intervals <- bind_rows(iv_sd, iv_md, iv_hl) |>
    mutate(across(where(is.logical), ~ tidyr::replace_na(.x, FALSE)))

  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, conc ~ time | treatment + id)
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
}
nca_parent <- run_nca("Cc")
nca_metab <- run_nca("Cc_metab")
```

## Comparison against published NCA

Published values are arithmetic means (median for tmax) of n = 6 per arm, from
Namour 2015 Tables 2 and 3. Table 3's C_t is the minimum concentration, which is
compared with PKNCA's `cmin`. The comparison table summarises the simulated
cohort by its median.

```{r nca-compare-parent}
pub_parent <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,      ~cmax, ~tmax, ~aucinf.obs, ~auclast, ~cmin, ~half.life,
  "SD 25 mg",       83.0,   2.5,        348,       NA,    NA,       5.72,
  "SD 50 mg",        247,     2,        771,       NA,    NA,       5.28,
  "SD 100 mg",       565,     2,       1743,       NA,    NA,       4.91,
  "SD 200 mg",      1160,     3,       4844,       NA,    NA,       5.68,
  "25 mg b.i.d.",    144,   0.5,         NA,      346,  3.75,       3.82,
  "50 mg b.i.d.",    211,   1.5,         NA,      758,  9.52,       5.75,
  "100 mg b.i.d.",   556,     3,         NA,     2380,  27.8,       5.87,
  "200 mg q.d.",    1200,     2,         NA,     4450,  6.04,       5.17,
  "300 mg q.d.",    1380,   1.5,         NA,     4400,  9.93,       10.9,
  "450 mg q.d.",    2580,   2.5,         NA,    10200,  17.6,       7.09
)
nca_units <- c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL",
               auclast = "ng*h/mL", cmin = "ng/mL", half.life = "h")
cmp_parent <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_parent, reference = pub_parent, by = "treatment",
  units = nca_units, tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_parent, caption = "Filgotinib: simulated (median) vs Namour 2015 Tables 2-3. * differs by >20%.")
```

```{r nca-check}
# Exposure check on the centre of the distribution across arms: a mis-read
# log-scale parameter (e.g. CL_P/F taken as 3.97 L/h instead of exp(3.97)) or
# a wrong FRAC orientation moves every AUC by tens of percent or more.
auc_pct <- function(res, pub) {
  s <- as.data.frame(res) |>
    filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "auclast")) |>
    group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
    summarise(sim = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  p <- pub |>
    select(treatment, aucinf.obs, auclast) |>
    pivot_longer(-treatment, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "pub") |>
    filter(!is.na(pub))
  inner_join(s, p, by = c("treatment", "PPTESTCD")) |>
    mutate(pct = 100 * (sim - pub) / pub)
}
auc_parent <- auc_pct(nca_parent, pub_parent)
auc_metab <- auc_pct(nca_metab, pub_metab)
stopifnot(
  nrow(auc_parent) == 10, nrow(auc_metab) == 10,
  abs(median(auc_parent$pct)) < 25,
  abs(median(auc_metab$pct)) < 15
)
# The empirical secondary pathway reproduces the plateau in metabolite
# exposure between 200 and 300 mg q.d. (Table 3: 69,900 vs 66,100 ng*h/mL).
m_auc <- setNames(auc_metab$sim, auc_metab$treatment)
stopifnot(abs(m_auc[["300 mg q.d."]] / m_auc[["200 mg q.d."]] - 1) < 0.15)
```

Metabolite AUC, Cmax, Cmin and single-dose half-life match Tables 2 and 3
closely, including the plateau in exposure between 200 and 300 mg q.d. The
metabolite half-life after repeated q.d. dosing is shorter than observed
(about 20 h against 26-27 h): a one-compartment metabolite with
CL_M/F = 2.83 L/h and V_M/F = 78.3 L has a single half-life of 19 h.

For filgotinib, Cmax and AUC are mostly within 20-40% of the published means,
which is reasonable for six-subject arithmetic means against a simulated
median. Three filgotinib quantities are starred systematically, and all three
follow from the published parameter values rather than from the encoding:

- **Tmax** is about 0.75 h against 2-3 h observed. With ka = 0.48 1/h and
  CL_P/F / V_C/F = 2.4 1/h, the typical profile peaks within the first hour.
  Namour 2015 reports that the model over-predicts "a number of samples ...
  taken shortly after dosing" and attributes this to "the limited data
  available in the absorption phase" (Results, discussion of Fig. 4).
- **Half-life** is about 12 h against 5-6 h observed. The PK model is
  two-compartmental, and its terminal phase (about 12 h for the typical
  subject) stays above the LLOQ in the simulated profiles. The paper's NCA
  half-lives used at least three points with adjusted R^2 >= 0.9 and vary
  widely across arms (3.8-10.9 h).
- **Cmin** is higher than observed (by up to about 85% at q.d. doses), as the
  longer terminal phase implies.

Table 6 is reproduced within about one percentage point (above), so the
pSTAT1 predictions the paper used for dose selection are unaffected by these
filgotinib NCA differences.

# Covariate effects

Two covariates change filgotinib exposure. Female sex (via V_C/F) changes only
the early profile. RA patient status raises the relative bioavailability by
21.6%, and body weight scales clearance. Typical steady-state exposures at
200 mg q.d.:

```{r covariates}
cov_cases <- tibble::tribble(
  ~case,                              ~WT, ~SEXF, ~DIS_RA,
  "Male healthy volunteer, 75 kg",     75,     0,       0,
  "Male healthy volunteer, 60 kg",     60,     0,       0,
  "Female RA patient, 65 kg",          65,     1,       1
) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()))
ev_cov <- tidyr::crossing(
  cov_cases,
  bind_rows(
    tibble(time = seq(0, 216, by = 24), amt = 200, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_),
    tibble(time = seq(216, 240, by = 0.1), amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  )
) |>
  mutate(DOSE_FILGOTINIB_MGD = 200) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
sim_cov <- solve_typical(ev_cov, keep = "case")
sim_cov |>
  group_by(case) |>
  summarise(
    `Filgotinib Cmax (ng/mL)` = signif(max(Cc), 3),
    `Filgotinib AUC0-24 (ng*h/mL)` = signif(sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2), 3),
    `Metabolite AUC0-24 (ng*h/mL)` = signif(sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc_metab, -1) + tail(Cc_metab, -1)) / 2), 4),
    `Mean pSTAT1 inhibition (%)` = signif(mean(100 * (1 - pstat1 / bl)), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(Subject = case) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical steady-state exposure and pSTAT1 inhibition at 200 mg q.d.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **FRAC orientation and scale.** The paper is internally inconsistent about
  what FRAC multiplies. Eq. 1 forms the metabolite at
  `FRAC * CL_P/F * C_P`, and the Table 4 legend defines FRAC as the "fraction
  of filgotinib metabolized to its active metabolite at the respective doses".
  The Results prose ("the fraction of filgotinib that is cleared through the
  secondary pathway") and Figure 3 (metabolite formation at
  `CL_P/V_C * (1 - FRAC)`) describe the complement. The model follows the
  equation and the table legend. Table 4 footnote b marks FRAC as
  "Probit-transformed", and the table prints the other transformed parameters
  on their transformed (log) scale. So 0.375 and 0.363 are taken as probit
  values, giving fm = pnorm(0.375) = 0.646 at 300 mg/day and 0.642 at
  450 mg/day. The alternative reading (FRAC = 0.375 as a secondary-pathway
  probability, fm = 0.625) gives almost the same exposure, but it reproduces
  Table 6 slightly less well at 300 mg q.d. (minimum / mean inhibition 58.1 /
  75.3% against the published 60.3 / 77.1%; this model gives 59.7 / 76.4%). The
  data also support fm of about 0.64: dose-normalised metabolite AUC at 300 and
  450 mg q.d. is 0.63 and 0.65 times that at 200 mg q.d. (Table 3).
- **FRAC as a dose-level covariate.** FRAC was estimated for the 300 mg q.d. and
  450 mg q.d. cohorts only, and every lower regimen has complete conversion.
  The model selects it from the total daily dose (`DOSE_FILGOTINIB_MGD`):
  fm = 1 below 300 mg/day, the 300 mg estimate from 300 to below 450 mg/day,
  and the 450 mg estimate from 450 mg/day upwards. The paper gives no basis
  for doses between the studied levels.
- **Weight centring.** The paper used centred power functions but does not report
  the centring weight. The maintainers used 75 kg, the weight of the typical
  subject in all of the paper's simulations, so that the model returns the
  published typical CL_P/F for that subject.
- **Form of the categorical effects.** The paper entered binary covariates "as
  factors" using PsN scm. The sex effect is encoded as
  `V_C/F * (1 + 2.95 * SEXF)` (male reference), the same `(1 + theta)` form the
  paper states for the RA effect on bioavailability. With these values,
  females have a 3.95-fold larger V_C/F. The paper notes that sex is confounded
  with study and patient status.
- **Residual error.** Eq. 1 and Table 4 give proportional error for both
  analytes. The Results text also says a combined additive/proportional error
  was retained for the metabolite, but no additive variance is reported, so
  the model follows the equation and table. The two proportional errors were
  estimated as correlated (covariance 0.0684, correlation 0.44). nlmixr2
  endpoints cannot share a correlated residual, so they are independent here.
  This affects only simulated observations with residual error, not
  individual predictions.
- **Metabolite mass units.** Eq. 1 has no molecular-weight conversion between
  parent and metabolite, so the metabolite is carried in filgotinib-mass
  equivalents and the ratio is absorbed into CL_M/F and V_M/F. `Cc_metab` is
  directly comparable with the measured metabolite ng/mL. The paper does not
  name the metabolite.
- **Virtual-cohort weights** are assumed (normal, mean 75 kg, SD 10 kg,
  truncated to 55-100 kg); the paper reports only the BMI inclusion range.
- **Errata and correspondence.** PubMed and Europe PMC list no erratum for this
  article (checked 2026-11-24). It drew a letter (Srinivas, Clin Pharmacokinet
  2015;54:1293-5, doi:10.1007/s40262-015-0335-6) and an author's reply
  (Namour, Clin Pharmacokinet 2015;54:1297-8, doi:10.1007/s40262-015-0336-5).
  The reply corrects no published value. It reports that a saturable
  pre-systemic conversion of filgotinib to the metabolite, added on top of the
  published secondary pathway, lowered the objective function by 14 points but
  could not replace that pathway, and that it would not have changed the dose
  selection. No parameter values are given for those alternative models, so
  this page implements the published model. The reply describes the published
  model as having a "dose-independent pre-systemic" conversion. Neither Eq. 1
  nor Table 4 contains such a component, and Eq. 1 as printed reproduces the
  paper's Table 6 simulations within about one percentage point (above).
